hero.credit: Photo: LERK / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

tldr: Get ONE T-money card — it pays for subway, bus, most taxis and convenience stores.
Tap in AND out (even on buses) to get free transfers within 30 minutes.
Navigate with Naver Map or KakaoMap — Google Maps transit barely works in Korea.
For taxis use Kakao T (upfront fare); for city-to-city use KTX/SRT high-speed rail.

highlights.title: One card does everything
highlights.body: A single rechargeable T-money card taps you onto the subway, buses, and most taxis — and even buys snacks at convenience stores. Buy it at any CU/GS25/7-Eleven or a station machine.

highlights.title: Use Korean map apps, not Google
highlights.body: Google Maps can't give driving/transit directions inside Korea. Install Naver Map or KakaoMap — both have English and real-time transit routing.

highlights.title: Transfers are free — if you tap out
highlights.body: Subway↔bus and bus↔bus transfers are free within 30 minutes with T-money. The catch: you must tap out on the bus too, or you lose the discount.

modes.title: Pick your mode
modes.intro: Four ways to move, and when each one wins. Precise fares are in the Verified-facts boxes above.

cards.name: Subway
cards.d: Fast, cheap, fully signposted in English, and traffic-proof. Seoul and Busan both have extensive networks. Start here for almost any city trip.

cards.name: City bus
cards.d: Colour-coded routes reach the gaps between stations. Tap in AND out. Great for short hops and scenic riverside or mountain routes.

cards.name: Taxi
cards.d: Cheap by global standards and everywhere. Call one with Kakao T for an upfront fare and no communication hassle.

cards.name: KTX / SRT
cards.d: High-speed rail reaches Busan in about 2h40 and Gyeongju, Daejeon, Gwangju and more. Book a seat ahead on weekends.

tmoney.title: The one card: T-money, step by step
tmoney.intro: T-money is a prepaid tap card. Here's the whole lifecycle — buy, top up, tap, and get your balance back.

steps.title: Buy the card
steps.detail: At any convenience store (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven, Emart24) or a subway station machine. Just say 'T-money, please'. The card itself costs a few thousand won and isn't refundable.

steps.title: Charge it with cash
steps.detail: Top up at the same convenience stores or the station recharge machines (they take cash). Load what you'll spend in a day or two; you can always add more.

steps.title: Tap in and out
steps.detail: Touch the card reader when you enter AND exit — on the subway gates and on the bus (both doors). Tapping out is what unlocks free transfers and correct fares.

steps.title: Refund the balance
steps.detail: Get leftover balance back at convenience stores (small balances) before you fly home. The card fee itself isn't refunded — only the remaining top-up.

tmoney.alt: Prefer not to manage a card? Many foreign travelers instead use WOWPASS (a prepaid card + T-money in one) or a registered credit card that supports contactless transit — but T-money is the simplest, most widely accepted option.

busColors.title: Decode the bus colours
busColors.intro: Seoul's buses are colour-coded by what they do — the colour tells you the route type at a glance.
busColors.credit: Photo: STA3816 / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0

items.name: Blue — Trunk
items.d: Long routes linking major districts across the city.

items.name: Green — Feeder
items.d: Short neighbourhood routes that connect you to the nearest subway station.

items.name: Yellow — Circular
items.d: Loops around the city centre and tourist areas (e.g. around Namsan).

items.name: Red — Wide-area express
items.d: Fast buses to satellite cities (Bundang, Ilsan). Higher fare.

taxi.title: Taxis & Kakao T
taxi.intro: Taxis are affordable and plentiful. The one thing to install is Kakao T — over 90% of Seoul taxis run on it, it shows an estimated fare before you confirm, and it removes any language or route-padding worry.
taxi.credit: Photo: Ilya Plekhanov / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

types.name: Regular (medium)
types.d: The standard orange/silver taxi. Metered; late-night surcharge up to 40% (~23:00–02:00).

types.name: Deluxe (mobeom)
types.d: Black with a gold stripe. Pricier, roomier, and NO late-night surcharge — good for late trips.

types.name: International taxi
types.d: Black or orange, marked 'International'. Drivers speak English/Chinese/Japanese; can be pre-booked.

taxi.tip: Pay by T-money or card in most taxis. Have your destination in Korean (the map app shows it) to make pickup and drop-off smooth.

intercity.title: City to city: KTX vs SRT
intercity.intro: Two high-speed rail operators cover the country. They're similar to ride — the difference is the departure station and a few rules.
intercity.imgAlt: A KTX high-speed train at Seoul Station
intercity.credit: Photo: Wikimedia Commons contributor · CC BY-SA 4.0

rows.label: Network
vals: Widest — Busan, Gyeongju, Gwangju, Gangneung, Yeosu…

intercity.note: Double-check WHICH station you depart from — arriving at Seoul Station for an SRT train (which leaves Suseo) is a classic, trip-ruining mistake. Book ahead for weekends and holidays.

items.name: Naver Map
items.d: The most complete map + transit + walking directions in Korea. English available.

items.name: KakaoMap
items.d: Excellent alternative map with clear transit routing and bus arrival times.

items.name: Kakao T
items.d: Call taxis with an upfront fare estimate; also bikes, and more.

items.name: Korail Talk
items.d: Official KTX booking app — reserve seats and show mobile tickets.

pitfalls.title: Mistakes that cost you time or money

items.d: It won't route transit or driving in Korea. Use Naver Map or KakaoMap instead.

items.t: Not tapping out on the bus
items.d: Skip the exit tap and you lose the free transfer and may be overcharged. Always tap both ways.
KTX leaves Seoul Station; SRT leaves Suseo. Confirm your departure station before you go.
Seoul subway is packed ~08:00–09:30 and ~18:00–19:30. Avoid big luggage at those times.
Buses don't give change well and some don't take cash. A charged T-money card avoids all of it.

items.q: Do I really need a T-money card?
items.a: It's the easiest option by far — one tap for subway, bus and most taxis, plus free transfers. Buy and charge it at any convenience store.

items.q: Which map app should I use?
items.a: Naver Map or KakaoMap. Google Maps can't provide transit or driving directions inside Korea due to data-export rules.
With T-money, transfers between subway and bus (or bus and bus) are free within 30 minutes — as long as you tap in and out every time.

items.q: How do I take a taxi without speaking Korean?
items.a: Use Kakao T: set your destination in the app, see the fare estimate, and the driver gets the route. Pay by card or T-money.
Both are fast (~2h40). KTX leaves central Seoul Station and is easiest to book (Korail Talk app); SRT is a bit cheaper but leaves Suseo Station and is harder to book with a foreign card.

items.q: Is the subway safe late at night?
items.a: Yes, Korea's transit is very safe. Note the subway stops running around midnight — after that, use a taxi (Kakao T) or a night (N) bus.
